result:
**Verdict: PASS.** I accepted both open Low findings, F-DG5-120 and F-DG5-121, as observations to be fixed in DG6, and raised no new findings.

**Candidate.** A complete, non-shallow clone at 660f40c gives `sha256:55a411ae…3a24ce` (2207 files) at both the start and the end of my run. This is the same candidate my round-2 record reviewed. The repository HEAD (eff0c25) is later than the source commit, but the commits since then change only delivery records, so the recomputed candidate ID is the one that counts. The historical validators for DG4, DG3, DG2 and DG1 pass, and so does the DG5 register check (`--register DG5`).

**Findings** (both Low, not mandatory, owner frontend-ux-engineer):
- **F-DG5-120: Arabic scoring-weight labels on the English Studio Elements table.**
  - **Confirmed.** Migration 0062 seeds these rows with no English label, and the label function falls back to Arabic.
  - **Why it's not blocking.** That function is used only in the administrator's Studio Elements table. The weights editor and every transformation-facing screen (weight sets, scorecard, rankings) take their labels from translation files instead. My round-2 screenshot shows "Strategic fit: 30% … Time-to-value: 15%" in English on the prioritization page. No server-side scoring, ranking or publish code reads these labels. No DG5 acceptance text covers this table's label language.
  - **DG6 fix.** Fall back to the source English label, or seed an English label through a new migration rather than editing 0062. Prefill the English label in the Edit dialog the same way, and add a component test.
  - **Cosmetic aside.** The Studio says "Time to value" where B0076 says "Time-to-value". I put this in the follow-up note, not in a new finding.
- **F-DG5-121: "Changed" shown for unchanged weights, and the rubric diff shown as raw JSON.**
  - **Confirmed.** The "Changed" column actually means "this version holds its own row". The editor saves all five weights, so all five read "Changed". Rubric levels are printed as JSON.
  - **Why it's not blocking.** The side-by-side diff is computed from the real values and lists exactly the changes: strategic_fit 25 → 30, financial_value 25 → 20, and the Feasibility rubric. The compatibility check lists the same three, so a Studio reviewer still sees a complete, accurate change list. REQ-S06-007 and REQ-S06-008 passed on this candidate in round 2, and no data, version pinning or approval is affected.
  - **DG6 fix.** Show "Changed" only where the value differs from the base version (or relabel the column), show rubric changes as readable before/after text in English and Arabic, and add tests.

**What I re-ran and what I cited.** This round I only re-ran the candidate checks, the validators and a code inspection of the two findings. All 78 requirements rest on my round-2 evidence for this same, unchanged candidate, as the assignment allows. The record restates every failure line in those logs:
- two failed checks in my own round-2 probe, which I corrected and re-ran successfully;
- a Playwright reporter message that followed them;
- a wrapper script that reported exit 1 although both runs' own logs end with exit 0;
- three npm configuration warnings.

There were no skipped, retried, flaky or timed-out tests.

**Other notes.**
- The four environmental residuals (live registry, live CI, Keycloak/demo IdP, AI and notification adapters) are recorded as PASS on their offline and configuration surface.
- While checking the sidecar format, I briefly saw round 2's (previous round) QA verifications file. It covers only F-DG5-140, played no part in my judgement, and is disclosed in the record. I read no other reviewer's round-3 record.
- The disposable clone has been removed.

Files are in `docs/delivery/`:
- `reviews/DG5/round-3/domain-reviewer.json`
- `reviews/DG5/round-3/domain-reviewer.verifications.json`
- `test-evidence/DG5/domain/round-3/` (evidence logs)
